studies.finding: Nuclear size increases during mitosis in control cells, but the increase is suppressed in Cutin-1-treated cells and the extension of the nucleus along its long axis is inhibited; both defects and a slight metaphase-anaphase delay (16.5 against 12.5 min of Cut11-GFP at the spindle pole body) are suppressed by the fas1-AT mutation. Spindles become curved and buckled in anaphase. In 13 of 25 filmed treated cells, chromosomes begin to segregate, fail to separate further and re-associate before septation, giving the cut phenotype, and nucleoli frequently remain unseparated. Chromosome defects appear about 3 h after Cutin-1, after nuclear and cell size fall within 1 h, and are reduced in cdc25-22 cells with enlarged nuclei (16.1 against 36.3 percent) and increased in wee1-50 cells with smaller nuclei (64.9 percent). The authors propose that fatty acid synthase-mediated nuclear envelope expansion provides the nuclear volume and elongation needed for chromosome segregation during closed mitosis.
limitations: One yeast with a closed mitosis; in organisms whose nuclear envelope breaks down, daughter nuclei form differently.
Fatty acid synthase is inhibited chemically; the existing nucleus and its envelope persist, and what fails is the expansion and division of the nuclear compartment.
About half of the filmed treated cells still segregate their chromosomes.
Lipid synthesis and membrane amounts are not measured in cells; the target identification section was read only through the Abstract.

studies.finding: PWWP-deficient hMutSα restores mismatch repair to NALM6 extracts in vitro, but PWWP mutants of hMSH6 form significantly fewer chromatin foci in cells. SETD2 knockdown lowers H3K36me3 and S-phase hMSH6 and hMSH2 foci; 4 of 14 knockdown HeLa subclones (28.6 percent) show microsatellite instability against none of the controls, and the spontaneous HPRT mutation frequency rises 18-fold, from 6.9 x 10^-7 to 1.2 x 10^-5, about 10-fold below that of hMSH6-deficient DLD-1 cells; the knockdown cells' extracts are not defective in mismatch repair in vitro, and SETD2 knockdown leaves the mutation frequency of hMSH6-deficient DLD-1 cells essentially unchanged. studies.finding: Inhibiting myosin phosphatase with M130Ab induces stress fibres and focal adhesions in starved cells, and MBS296 blocks serum-induced stress-fibre and focal-adhesion formation and keeps MLC phosphorylation low while a microfilament network still forms; the control fragment has no effect. Y-27632 blocks M130Ab-induced stress fibres in the cell centre, leaving peripheral MLCK-associated bundles, and with ML-9 added the peripheral bundles are not induced either. In cells growing in serum, Y-27632 disassembles stress fibres (uninjected cells in Figure 5k), whereas ML-9 does not markedly affect them. The authors conclude that MLC phosphorylation is necessary and sufficient for stress-fibre and focal-adhesion assembly, ROCK acting in the cell centre and MLCK at the periphery.
limitations: One fibroblast line; structures are assessed in images with stated numbers of injected cells, and the disassembly of existing fibres by Y-27632 in uninjected cells is reported qualitatively, confirming an earlier report.
10 µM pharmacological kinase inhibitors may act off target.
Actin polymerization into a microfilament network continues when MLC phosphorylation is blocked; intracellular transport is not measured.
